archetypes.name: caller-enumeration
archetypes.rationale: The plan moves sentinel ownership from emit-design-plan-preview.sh to run-step3-review.sh but the scope list may not enumerate every call site of --variant step3 or .step3-entry-plan-printed; a missed caller would silently re-introduce the old behavior alongside the new driver ownership.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether the plan's scope list and modification targets cover every caller of `emit-design-plan-preview.sh --variant step3` and every consumer or writer of the `.step3-entry-plan-printed` sentinel across the repository — not only in the listed scope files but in any SKILL.md region, hook, wrapper script, or integration harness outside that list. Verify no call site the plan omits still carries the old sentinel logic, which would cause double-render on first entry or never-render on re-entry alongside the new driver ownership. Also check whether `docs/issue-anchored-plan.md` or any other doc explicitly describes the separate preview turn and is absent from the Step 6 drift-sweep enumeration. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: fd-routing-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan's central mechanical claim — that capturing emit-design-plan-preview.sh stdout via $() then re-emitting through emit writes to FD 3 after larch_quiet_init — must match the actual quiet-lib implementation; an incorrect model silently routes the preview to the swallowed log instead of the orchestrator.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify the plan's FD-routing model against the actual quiet-lib implementation: after `larch_quiet_init` redirects FD 1 to the quiet log and sets `exec 3>&1`, does a subshell launched via `$()` inside `run-step3-review.sh` inherit the FD 3 assignment, and does calling `emit "$_preview_out"` in the parent shell then write to FD 3 as the plan states? Check `scripts/lib-quiet.md` and the live `emit`/`larch_quiet_init` source to confirm FD 3 is open and inheritable at that call point, and verify the `LARCH_QUIET_DISABLE` edge case described in the plan (emit routes to FD 1, still captured by `$()`) is consistent with how `emit` actually selects its output descriptor. Flag any divergence between the plan's routing description and the code's actual FD assignments that would cause the preview to silently disappear. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
